problem: The sentence 'They give checkpoints without pretending a review consumes no time' is confusing and reads as if it contradicts the zero-duration definition just given. A student can take away that a milestone itself takes time, or that milestones hide review work.
fix: Say it plainly: 'A milestone is a zero-duration marker for a finished event, such as design frozen or user acceptance signed off. The review that produces the event is a normal task with its own duration; the milestone only marks the moment it ends.'

where: Section 1, Duration ≈ Effort ÷ People formula note
problem: 'Add roughly 10–20% for coordination when People is more than 1' does not say what to add it to. A student may add 10–20% to people, or to effort, instead of to the duration.
fix: 'When People is more than 1, increase the duration by roughly 10–20%: Duration ≈ (Effort ÷ People) × 1.1 to 1.2, in working days.'

where: Exam traps, fourth bullet, and Quiz Q6
problem: 'Float' is used as a synonym for slack without ever being defined, so a student meeting the word in an exam paper may not connect it to the slack defined in Section 2.
fix: At first use write: 'Tasks in series share the same slack (also called float), so two tasks showing 4 days each give the path 4 days, not 8.'
